The First Heroes.text: The first heroes were ordinary people with Quirks who began protecting others on their own, before any license existed. During the chaos years some borrowed the idea from old comics: they took names, wore costumes, stopped robberies and pulled people from wrecks. They broke the law to do it, and many were hurt or arrested, but the public loved them, and in many towns they were the only help that came. Japan chose to license them rather than prosecute them: the best received legal standing, government pay and rules to follow, and the word hero passed from the street into the law. Those who refused the license or could not meet its standards became the first people the system called vigilantes. Hero history classes still open with these figures.
